## Top Ten Longest Baseball Careers

__Write an SQL query that pulls the tables you need into a polars dataframe using nothing more than SELECT and FROM statements. Then, use python polars to identify the top 10 players with the longest Major League Baseball careers.__

_The table below contains Information on the ten players who played baseball the longest. After research, it was found that these players could have played so long only because they started out young. The player who debuted the oldest out of these is Charley O'Leary at 28 years old, and the youngest being Nolan Ryan at only 19 years old. Hence, if you have a dream of being the longest playing MBA player but have reached your late thirties, you may want to rethink your goals and aspirations. On top of that, all of these ten players began in or before the 20th century, likely meaning that modern baseball players have a shorter (however higher paying, see Unit 3 Task 3 Question 2). The average career for these players was impressive, seeing that the average career length for most sports is no more than ten years. These impressive players seemed to have made their baseball careers look like a white collar career._
```{python}
query1 = """
SELECT playerID, yearID
FROM appearances
"""
query2 = """
SELECT playerID, nameFirst AS first_name, nameLast AS last_name
FROM people
"""
df = pl.read_database(query1,con)
adf = pl.read_database(query2,con)
df = (
    df.join(
        adf,
        on=["playerID"],
        how="inner"
    )
    .group_by(["playerID","first_name","last_name"])
    .agg((pl.col("yearID").max()-pl.col("yearID").min()+1).cast(pl.Int8).alias("career_length_years"))
).sort(by=["career_length_years"], descending=True)
df.head(10)
```

## Best Paying Baseball Positions

__Write an SQL query that pulls the tables you need into a polars dataframe. Then, use python polars to create a summary table showing the average salary for each position (e.g., pitcher, catcher, outfielder). Position information can be found in the fielding table in the POS column.__

_Seen below is a table of most common baseball positions and their salary information. This information is gathered by finding each individual player's most common position and aggregating that. The table is organized by the most common position, and information on highest and average salary can be seen alongside it. Most average salaries are in the lower millions range, however still quite a substantial salary. Most high salaries are in the twenty millions and some even in the thirties. Most high salaries are even numbers, however the highest salary of 27,328,046 belongs to Yoenis Cespedes, and after research it was found that the database lists him as paid that exact amount for the year 2016._
```{python}
query1 = """
SELECT playerID, POS AS position
FROM fielding
"""
query2 = """
SELECT playerID, salary
FROM salaries
"""
replacers = {
    "P": "Pitcher",
    "1B": "First Base",
    "2B": "Second Base",
    "3B": "Third Base",
    "SS": "Shortstop",
    "C": "Catcher",
    "OF": "Outfield",
    "DH": "Designated Hitter"
}
df = pl.read_database(query1,con)
adf = pl.read_database(query2,con)
df = (
    df.group_by(["playerID","position"])
    .len(name="count")
    .sort(by=["playerID","count"], descending=[False,True])
    .group_by("playerID")
    .head(1)
    .drop("count")
)
df = (
    df.join(
        adf,
        on="playerID",
        how="inner"
    )
    .with_columns(pl.col("position").replace(replacers))
    .group_by("position")
    .agg(
        (pl.col("salary").n_unique().cast(pl.Int16)).alias("total_players"),
        (pl.col("salary").max().cast(pl.Int32)).alias("highest_salary"),
        (pl.col("salary").mean().cast(pl.Int32)).alias("average_salary")
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("average_salary") > 3_000_000)
        .then(pl.lit("High Salary"))
        .when(pl.col("average_salary") > 2_000_000)
        .then(pl.lit("Medium Salary"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("Low Salary"))
        .alias("average_salary_ranked")
    )
    .sort(by=["total_players"],descending=True)
)
df
```
